GLOBAL_FINDINGS.finding: Per-song feature cell (25 YouTube mega-hits, G001-G025, uploads 2009-2018; secondary estimates): BPM as recorded median 110 (p25 91, p75 130; range 75-190 where 190 is a 12/8 count for 'Perfect'); 23/25 feature pages state a half- or double-time alternative, so perceived pulse is ambiguous for almost every hit; bands: <90 20%, 90-109 28%, 110-129 24%, 130-149 20%, >=150 8%.

Mode in the same cell: major 56% (14), minor 32% (8), modal 8% (D Dorian 'Uptown Funk', G Mixolydian 'Shake It Off'), null 1. Where both a Spotify-derived site key and a published sheet-music key were available (n=14), they disagreed in 7 cases, almost always by relative major/minor — site-only mode values are unreliable.

Duration in the cell (Wikipedia infobox, n=25): median 3:44 (224 s), p25 3:32, p75 3:56, min 2:25 ('Dame Tu Cosita'), max 4:41 ('Thinking Out Loud'). These 2009-2018 video mega-hits are longer than the 2024 Spotify charting average (~3:00, L07).

Published sheet-music vocal ranges (n=10, quoted on Wikipedia; not measured from recordings): span median 22 semitones (p25 17.5, p75 25.5; min 15 'Dark Horse', max 39 'Uptown Funk' incl. falsetto/ad-libs); lowest notes B2-B♭3 (median MIDI 52 ≈ E3), highest notes A4-D6 (median MIDI 73 ≈ C#5). Typical male-lead hits sit roughly E3-C#5 on paper.

Spotify-derived energy median 74 (n=24), danceability median 68 (n=24), valence median 45 (n=15, bimodal: 17-29 vs 69-96), loudness median -6 dB (n=15). Structural timing was stated on a page for only 2/25 songs (Blank Space: two-bar drum intro; Shake It Off: bridge 2:18-2:42); chorus arrival remains null for all rows.
Among the 40 most-streamed Spotify songs (as of 2026-09-13), 82.5% were released in 2012 or later; median release year 2016; a catalog tail (1983-2008) of 5 songs exists.

The 38 most-viewed music videos on YouTube (kworb) all exceed 3.1 bn views; median upload age of the 17 dated ones is ~4,325 days (~11.8 yr); descriptive views/day since upload median ~1.04 M. Longevity, not launch spikes, dominates all-time totals.
GLOBAL_FINDINGS.confidence: high for counts; medium for views/day (K4 undated)

GLOBAL_FINDINGS.finding: Cross-source overlap is thin: only 5 songs are in both the YouTube top-38 and Spotify top-40; only 1 (As It Was) is in both Spotify top-40 and the Hot 100 longest-#1 list. 'Exceptional performance' is platform-specific.
Hits shortened: Hot 100 avg ~3:30 by 2018 (-20 s in 5 yr); Spotify charting avg ~3:00 in 2024 (-30 s vs 2019); UK #1s back near 3:00 by 2022.
GLOBAL_FINDINGS.confidence: medium (consistent across 3 independent analyses; none peer-reviewed)

GLOBAL_FINDINGS.finding: Instrumental intros shrank from >20 s (mid-1980s) to ~5 s (2015) in US top-10 singles (n=303); tempo rose ~8% over the same period; but within-artist popular-vs-less-popular comparison showed no such pattern.
GLOBAL_FINDINGS.confidence: high for trend; trend is an era effect, not a success effect

GLOBAL_FINDINGS.finding: Late-2010s US top-5 hits averaged ~93 BPM (2017: 93.2; 2018: 92.6; modal 78-80 BPM); 43% of 2010s #1s were below 100 BPM vs 25% in 1960-1989. Half/double-time ambiguity is unresolved in these sources.

Minor-key share among US #1s rose from ~25% (pre-2000) to ~55% (post-2000); UK #1s 55-58% minor in 2019-2022. But #1s vs other charting songs differ little in mode (65/35 vs 63/37 major/minor) and tempo (117 vs 120 BPM).
GLOBAL_FINDINGS.confidence: medium for era shift; low for any success association

GLOBAL_FINDINGS.finding: Key changes nearly vanished (~25% of #1s in 1960s-90s; one in 2010-2020); fade-outs vanished after 2011 in UK #1s.

Lyrical repetition rose 1958-2017 and top-10 songs were more repetitive than the rest in every year; chorus repetition associated with higher probability of #1 and faster climb, with diminishing returns for excessive word repetition.
Hits are 'optimally differentiated': moderately atypical relative to the preceding 52 weeks' charting songs outperform highly typical ones (inverted-U).
Successful UK songs 1985-2015 were happier, more danceable/party-like, less relaxed and more 'female' than the average release, while the market as a whole trended sadder and less bright.

Melodies of US top-5 hits since 2000: ~2.8 notes/s, mean interval ~2 semitones, two-thirds of pitches within ~5.5 semitones (narrow tessitura); choruses use fewer notes and larger intervals than verses.
Tempo variability in hits collapsed after 1979 (median yearly CV 1.51 in 1972 to 0.03 in 1994): modern hits are grid-tight.

HINDI_FINDINGS.finding: India's most-viewed music videos (Wikipedia, as of 2026-02-18; n=40 song rows) are multilingual: Hindi 60%, Punjabi 17.5%, Haryanvi 5%, plus Tamil/Bhojpuri/Bengali mixes. Among Hindi-language rows, 74% are film songs; overall 60% film / 40% non-film.
Label concentration: T-Series uploaded 45% of the top-40 Indian music videos (18/40); Zee Music 10%; YRF 5%.
Upload years cluster 2016-2020 (2019 alone 24%); median upload age ~2,928 days (~8 yr); descriptive views/day median ~436 k — roughly 40% of the global top-video median.

Non-film videos show a slightly higher median views/day (466 k, n=14) than film videos (379 k, n=22) in this hit-only list; the cells are small and confounded by era and star presence — reported as frequency, not association.

Spotify India all-time chart totals (2019-02-27 to 2026-08-26, n=37 Indian songs in top-40) show two longevity archetypes: 17 peak-#1 songs (median chart days ~863) versus never-top-3 songs that stayed on the top-200 for 1,900-2,600 days (catalog ballads such as Tum Se Hi, Kabira, Tera Hone Laga Hoon, Dil Diyan Gallan).

73% of Spotify India top-40 titles carry no '(From "Film")' tag; the tag is unreliable as a film indicator (several untagged titles are film songs), so film-share on Spotify is unidentifiable from this source.

YouTube-view leaders and Spotify-India-stream leaders do not overlap (0 shared songs): Indian YouTube rewards dance/party and Punjabi/Haryanvi video hits; Spotify India totals are dominated by romantic ballads and independent singer-songwriters (Anuv Jain x3, King x2, Shubh x2).

Bollywood hits 1953-2013 (n=310): ~25% Asavari (natural-minor type), ~25% Bilawal (major), ~25% Bhairavi/Kafi/Khamaj (Phrygian/Dorian/Mixolydian-type), 8% pentatonic, 4% Kalyan; Kalyan declined since the 1960s, Bhairavi rose.
Hindi film songs shortened from 8+ min examples (1970s-80s) to 'often fade out after the four-minute mark'; no quantified India-specific duration dataset was found.

Billboard India Songs 2022 #1s: 9 titles on the page (7 in cohort after excluding Hanuman Chalisa and Pink Venom); longest runs were Punjabi (295: 18 wk; The Last Ride: 14 wk) and Telugu film (Srivalli: 9 wk); Hindi film Kesariya 3 wk. Only 2022 data are public on Wikipedia.

CROSSOVER_FINDINGS.finding: No Hindi/Indian recording appears in any global top list fetched (YouTube top-30/kworb top-40, Spotify top-40, Hot 100 longest #1s). Observed cross-market presence runs global->India only (Starboy, Perfect, Pink Venom).
CROSSOVER_FINDINGS.confidence: high for absence in these lists; says nothing about mid-tier crossover

CROSSOVER_FINDINGS.finding: Devotional recitation 'Shree Hanuman Chalisa' is the only Indian upload in the global top-30 (5.67 bn, W1); excluded from the song cohort but it is the strongest evidence that Indian repertoire can reach global-scale view counts through domestic volume plus daily repeat use (4.4 M views 'yesterday' on kworb).
GLOBAL_HINDI_CROSSOVER cohort is therefore empty (n=0). Reference principles for crossover below are editorial test directions, not empirical zones.

VOCAL_KEY_OPTIMIZER.purpose: Transpose a reference zone to Nitin's measured voice while preserving mode, interval structure, contour, groove, and structural principles. Absolute key of any reference song is NOT a recommendation.

inputs.reference_intervals_or_contour: relative pitch sequence (semitones from tonic) — no protected melody copied; used only as a range envelope
inputs.reference_chorus_peak_rel: semitones above tonic at chorus/climax peak
inputs.reference_verse_floor_rel: semitones above/below tonic at verse floor
inputs.nitin_climax_ceiling: highest note sustainable for >=2 s at full intensity, measured — CURRENTLY NULL

algorithm: 1. Express the reference zone's verse floor, verse ceiling, chorus peak and climax peak as semitone offsets from its tonic (mode preserved).
2. For candidate tonics T in the 12 pitch classes across plausible octaves, map each offset to absolute MIDI notes.
3. Constraint A (hard): all verse notes within nitin_comfortable_tessitura.
5. Preference C: chorus peak sits 2-5 semitones above the verse ceiling but below passaggio, or fully above passaggio if the artist's measured mix is stable there.
6. Preference D: guitar/keyboard-friendly tonic if live performance matters (L13 shows key distribution skew, not a success effect).
7. Output ranked tonics with a FIT score = null until measurements exist; report the transposition interval only.

audition_protocol.safety: Warm up 10-15 min; no pushing past discomfort; stop at strain; sessions <=30 min; hydration; measure on 3 separate days at different times.
measurements: Lowest comfortable sustained note (>=3 s, stable pitch) — piano/tuner reference
Highest comfortable sustained note in chest/mix at speaking-level dynamic
Highest comfortable belt/mix note at performance dynamic (>=2 s)
Highest head-voice note usable in the song's style
Passaggio region: sing a 5-note ascending scale on /a/ and note where the voice wants to flip
Tessitura test: sing a 3-minute known song in three keys (original, -2, +2) and rate fatigue 1-5 after each
Record each take (44.1 kHz WAV) with a metronome tag; log MIDI note numbers, date, time, and fatigue rating
audition_protocol.output: nitin_comfortable_tessitura, nitin_climax_ceiling, nitin_passaggio; recorded in UNCHAINED_NITIN_OWN_DATA with recording_id and metric_timestamp

SCORING_ENGINE_DESIGN.status: DESIGN ONLY — not executed; no hit probability; no calibrated prediction (hit-only samples cannot calibrate).

SUCCESS_SIGNAL_SCORE.definition: count-based alignment with evidence-supported zones (Z1-Z8): +1 per satisfied zone criterion with supporting_n>=300, +0.5 per criterion with lower n; reported as 'k of m criteria', never a probability

EVIDENCE_CONFIDENCE.definition: min over used criteria of {high, medium-high, medium, low}; plus n_null inputs

REFERENCE_MATCH_SCORE.definition: per zone: fraction of zone fields (bpm band, mode, chorus arrival band, duration band, repetition band) matched by the input; returns null for zones whose fields are null

NITIN_FIT_SCORE.definition: from VOCAL_KEY_OPTIMIZER; null until tessitura measured

EXPECTED_RETENTION_PROFILE.definition: emitted ONLY if UNCHAINED_NITIN_OWN_DATA contains observed YouTube retention curves for >=5 prior publications; otherwise null with reason 'no observed retention data'

RISKS.definition: list: e.g. 'chorus arrival >60 s (L09/L17)', 'duration >4:00 vs streaming era trend (L07)', 'key change present (L12)', 'excessive word repetition (L24)', 'highly typical profile (L05)', 'climax above measured ceiling'

COMPARABLE_SONGS.definition: nearest rows in RAW_DATASET by available fields; with feature fields null for 167/168 rows the comparables are by success-signal shape and release_type only

explicitly_not_output: any numeric score without listed evidence ids

ID_AND_ATTRIBUTION_CHAIN.note: Proposed schema only. No access to, or claim about, any existing private architecture.

entities.content_id: derivative asset (video edit, short, lyric video, live clip) -> recording_id
entities.publication_id: content_id x platform x upload timestamp x official flag
entities.experiment_id: A/B or sequential test -> publication_ids, hypothesis, pre-registered metric
entities.lead_id: inbound inquiry -> attributed publication_id(s) with evidence type (link click, stated source, UTM)
entities.revenue_event_id: payout/stream royalty/booking fee -> booking_id or publication_id, amount, currency, timestamp

metrics.publication_metric: (publication_id, metric_name, value, metric_timestamp, source_api) — views, watch_hours, avg_view_duration, retention_curve, subscribers_gained, streams, saves, skips

ID_AND_ATTRIBUTION_CHAIN.flow: musical parameters (recording_id) -> song_id -> content_id -> publication_id -> publication_metrics (views, watch hours, retention, subscriber conversion) -> streams (publication/recording) -> lead_id -> booking_id -> revenue_event_id
rules: watch hours only from platform analytics exports, never views x duration
every metric row carries metric_timestamp and source

tools_used: no paid tools, no downloads of copyrighted audio, no credentials
